Summary: The change is documentation only, in one commit. Decision 38, the Stack 10 audit record, TODO.md, the 0.2.10 audit row in SECURITY.md and an Unreleased CHANGELOG entry now say the gate template is public under the MIT licence, with TACE Data Management Inc. as the copyright holder, and that its licence file is the only file in it that names TACE. I followed the order in Docs/REVIEW.md. For intent, I checked the commit message against the diff and checked the edited documents against each other and against the rest of decision 38. There are no tests or code to review. For S-16, the company name already appears in the module manifest and in every file header, so naming it here discloses nothing new, and the change names no template repository, host or account. One stale statement remains in decision 38.

Findings.Title: Decision 38 now says the template is public, but its Rejected clause still turns down a git submodule because the target's CI 'could not reach a private template'.
Findings.Detail: The amended decision 38 says the template 'is public and released under the MIT licence'. The same row still gives this reason for rejecting a git submodule: 'the target's CI could not reach a private template'. Now that the template is public, that reason no longer holds as written, so the decision contradicts itself. The reader cannot tell whether the subtree choice still stands or why. The change edits this row and should have updated the clause too. Fix: reword the reason so it still holds, for example that the template was private when the decision was made, or that a subtree keeps the target's CI free of any dependency on the template repository. Or record that the reason has changed.
